title: Finding a work order by its customer's name still works
custom_preconds:
SEEDED DATA REQUIRED. Seed the Global Search regression dataset before running this case - the exact values are in build/global-search/v1-coverage-audit-2026-09-10/seed-data.json (seed_global_search_dataset.py creates it). Every keyword below is unique to one field, so a hit proves that field is searchable.

Access needed:
- Work Orders: view

Seeded record used by this case:
- Customer "ZZAUTOTEST Bridgeport Hauling"
- Work orders WO-A to WO-D, all for that customer
custom_steps:
1. Confirm the seeded customer and their work orders exist.
2. Open global search.
3. Type: Bridgeport
4. Look at the Work Orders group.
custom_expected:
1. The seeded customer's work orders are listed under the Work Orders group.
2. You did not need to know any work order number to find them.
3. This proves the customer name still matches work orders, not only customer records.

Based on the Global Search V2 PRD v1.2 (Confluence version 12), which is SILENT on this behaviour, so Standing Rule 96 keeps the V1 behaviour as an invariant that must not change. V1 behaviour established from the ShopView code baseline 55767168 (FetchDataQueryHandler.php:91-118 - the customer name was concatenated into the work order search text). Not yet checked against any V2 build - no Global Search QA build exists.
